n: Fourth vision: a basket of ripe summer fruit, gathered at the end of the growing season.

f.g: Hebrew qayitz — late-summer fruit such as figs.

n: A wordplay: “summer fruit” (qayitz) sounds like “end” (qetz). Israel is ripe — its end has come. God will no longer overlook its sins.

f.g: Hebrew qetz, a pun on qayitz (summer fruit).

f.w: I will not again pass by them

n: Temple songs will turn into wailing, and dead bodies will be everywhere, thrown out in stunned silence.

f.g: Or “Hush!” — the same word as in Amos 6:10.

n: Amos again targets those who trample the needy and try to wipe out the poor.
Merchants can’t wait for holy days to end so they can get back to cheating: shrinking the measure, inflating the price, and rigging the scales. Their religion is only outward.

f.w: making the ephah small, and the shekel great
f.g: Using a smaller measure for grain sold and a heavier weight for silver received — cheating both ways.

n: They buy the poor into slavery for a trifle and sell sweepings of wheat as if it were good grain.

f.g: Chaff and husks swept up from the floor.

n: God swears He will never forget what they have done. Sin that is not repented of remains on the record.

f.g: Ironically, God swears by Israel’s pride — something as fixed as His own being — or by Himself, “the Pride of Jacob.”

n: Because of this, the whole land will heave like the Nile in flood, rising and sinking. An earthquake may be in view.

f.g: The Nile, which rose and fell every year.

n: The sun will set at noon and darkness will fall in broad daylight. A solar eclipse visible in Israel in 763 BC may have given this image force.

f.w: cause the sun to go down at noon

n: Celebrations will turn to funerals. People will wear sackcloth and shave their heads, mourning as for an only son.

f.g: Shaving the head was a mourning custom.

n: A sobering prophecy: a famine not of food but of hearing God’s word. Latter-day Saints often see this fulfilled in the Great Apostasy, when prophets and priesthood authority were withdrawn.

f.w: hearing the words of the LORD

n: People will search everywhere, from sea to sea, but will not find the word of the Lord. Revelation is a gift that can be lost.
Even the strongest, healthiest young people will faint from thirst — spiritual and physical.
Those who swear by the idols of Samaria, Dan, and Beersheba will fall and not rise. False worship cannot save.

f.g: Probably a goddess or the calf idol worshiped there.
Literally “the way to Beersheba” — the pilgrimage route, perhaps meaning its deity.
